content:
Rafael Mendes: flagging a concern from SRE side on the new auto-stop behavior (hard-stop) for route experiments. can we get a kill switch that disables *all* auto-stop actions quickly if we see false positives in prod?

Jada Williams: +1. with guardrails reading p99 + error rate from the rollup, if the rollup lags or we get partial attribution we could accidentally stop an experiment.

Allison Grant: we already have the “soft-stop” path (mark degraded + notify) — but the hard-stop PR adds an optional stop transition when severe thresholds trip. seems like we need an emergency off switch regardless.

Jordan Lee: what kind of kill switch are you thinking? feature flag? config field? env var?

Rafael Mendes: something that on-call can flip without a deploy. ideally:
- global override: hard-stop disabled across all regions
- takes effect fast (minutes)
- doesn’t require Console writes (in case control plane is having issues)

Dylan Brooks: from Console POV we can expose an “Auto-stop enabled” toggle per experiment, but that doesn’t solve the “global emergency” angle.

Sean Gallagher: SRE ask is specifically global + fast. we can’t be in a world where a noisy metric pipeline causes cascading stops and we can’t stop it.

Caleb Johnson: re false positives: we saw some p99 spikes in staging tied to the retry path where attribution was missing (metrics were undercounting success, overcounting errors). if that lands in prod, guardrail eval could be wrong.

Jada Williams: yep, and when attribution drop happens the per-variant rollup can get weird. auto-stop should be conservative but we should still have the “break glass” switch.

Jordan Lee: implementation idea: add a dynamic config key checked by the guardrail evaluator worker before issuing STOP. e.g. `experiments.autostop.hard_stop_enabled` default false. if false, evaluator can still emit “would_have_stopped” metric / banner but won’t execute mutation.

Allison Grant: + also add a second layer on the control plane API side (stop endpoint) to require a header/actor? but that’s more for human-initiated. for auto-stop, gating in evaluator makes sense.

Rafael Mendes: evaluator gating is good. but we should avoid dependency on the exact same config store that might be degraded. can we read from the existing feature flag service (the one used for beta allowlists) which is already replicated?

Connor O'Brien: we can thread it through the same feature flag system as route experiments enablement (`route_experiments_enabled`). add `route_experiments_autostop_enabled` as a separate flag. on-call can flip it in the flag console.

Jordan Lee: that works. guardrail evaluator reads flag every N seconds (cached) and logs the current value w/ config version.

Jada Williams: do we also need a per-experiment knob? I’d still like to support “hard-stop for this experiment only” later, but global flag should override.

Dylan Brooks: propose precedence:
1) global kill switch OFF => no hard-stop anywhere
2) experiment config `auto_stop_mode` (off | soft | hard)
3) route defaults

Allison Grant: sounds right. also please emit a metric like `experiment_guardrail_autostop_blocked_total{reason="global_kill_switch"}` so we can see if we’re suppressing real stops.

Rafael Mendes: +1 and write a tiny runbook section: “If auto-stop appears to be firing incorrectly, disable `route_experiments_autostop_enabled`” + link in the alert payload.

Sean Gallagher: requirements from SRE before we sign off:
- kill switch is global, replicated, and editable by on-call (SRE + platform oncall) without deploy
- hard-stop is OFF by default for beta
- when disabled, evaluator must not attempt the stop mutation at all (not even best-effort)
- add an audit log / change record for toggling the flag (even if it’s in the flag system)

Connor O'Brien: on the flag change audit: feature flag service already keeps actor + timestamp. we can link it in the internal runbook.

Jordan Lee: for the “not attempt stop mutation”: we’ll short-circuit before calling experiment service. we can still send notification “guardrail breached but auto-stop suppressed by global setting.”

Jada Williams: ok. we should also make sure the kill switch affects both “latency regression hard-stop” and any future hard-stop conditions (quality regression etc). name should be generic.

Dylan Brooks: naming: `route_experiments_hard_stop_enabled` maybe clearer. and we can add `route_experiments_hard_stop_kill_switch` but that’s redundant.

Sean Gallagher: prefer `route_experiments_hard_stop_enabled` with default false. that’s your kill switch.

Allison Grant: +1. also make sure the Console UI copy doesn’t imply hard-stop is guaranteed if the global flag disables it (banner/tooltip: “Hard-stop subject to org/admin policy”).

Rafael Mendes: cool. can we get an owner? I can open a quick follow-up ticket but sounds like Jada/Jordan area.

Jordan Lee: I’ll take the implementation in evaluator + wiring to flag service. will loop in Rafael for runbook text.

Jada Williams: I’ll handle the experiment config precedence + message in notifications (so users understand why it didn’t stop).

Sean Gallagher: SRE sign-off contingent on the above. once there’s a PR, tag me + Rafael for review. :thumbsup:

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. I’ll start a short runbook patch + alert text update once the flag name is final.
